diagnosis.headline: Create the capability from the empty seed: a prompt.md stating the grader's value contract (data_only=True, no recalculation => write literal values, not formulas) plus a task_template.md that deletes the harmful 'once that file exists, you are done' line and replaces it with a 4-step procedure whose step 3 is a mandatory grader-identical read-back. Content transferred verbatim from the project's read-only prior run (reused_seed_run cand_0003), which measured val 1.000 on this identical 40-task split and held-out test 0.875 vs seed 0.386, after independent re-verification against the scorer source and all 40 trajectories.

clusters.name: Formula written into answer cells
clusters.detail: compare_workbooks (third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py:155) opens both workbooks with openpyxl.load_workbook(data_only=True), and the primary metric hard_no_recalc is computed on the file AS THE AGENT SAVED IT (adapter.py:1581, before _recalc_workbook runs). A formula written through openpyxl carries no cached value, so the grader reads None and every answer cell is wrong even when the formula logic is perfect. A mechanical scan of all 40 trajectories finds a formula write in 24 of 26 failures and in only 1 of 14 passes (6698, which passed solely by hand-injecting cached <v> elements into the sheet XML).

clusters.name: No verification round; stops at 'a file exists'
clusters.detail: The adapter's built-in task template says 'Final solution code that writes the modified spreadsheet file to output_path -- once that file exists, you are done.' Every one of the 26 failing traces ends with the identical pair save(output_path) -> '[Code executed successfully with no output]' -> 'Done'. Not one re-opened its own output file. The instruction surface was telling the agent that producing a wrong-but-present file is completion.

clusters.name: Excel error text or wrong Python type in answer cells
clusters.detail: compare_cell_value normalises both sides via transform_value (numerics -> round(float(v),2); numeric strings coerced; datetime -> Excel serial rounded to a whole day; time -> 'HH:MM:SS'; None == '') and then fails outright on type(v1) != type(v2). Traces write '#N/A' error strings and text where a number or a real datetime was expected.

clusters.name: Wrote outside the answer, or over the user's worked example
clusters.detail: The whole answer range is compared cell by cell, and for cells the instruction does not ask about the gold holds the cell's own original input value. 50768 filled 9 of 9 cells where the gold has only 3; 48588 overwrote 17 cells whose expected value is the cell's own original input (the user's hand-made example, 'as I have manually done in Column B').

clusters.name: Moment-vs-span counting semantics
clusters.detail: A column labelled with a single moment ('still open at month end') computed as 'open at any point during the period', which is always the larger quantity. 43436 wrote exactly the span predicate and its feedback is the uniform-overcount signature: '5 cell(s) hold a number HIGHER than expected'.

clusters.name: Formula written into answer cells

A formula written through openpyxl carries no cached value, so the grader reads None and every answer cell is wrong even when the formula logic is perfect. A mechanical scan of all 40 trajectories finds a formula write in 24 of 26 failures and in only 1 of 14 passes (6698, which passed solely by hand-injecting cached <v> elements into the sheet XML).

clusters.name: No verification round; stops at 'a file exists'
clusters.detail: The adapter's built-in task template says 'Final solution code that writes the modified spreadsheet file to output_path -- once that file exists, you are done.' Every one of the 26 failing traces ends with the identical pair save(output_path) -> '[Code executed successfully with no output]' -> 'Done'. Not one re-opened its own output file. The instruction surface was telling the agent that producing a wrong-but-present file is completion.

clusters.name: Excel error text or wrong Python type in answer cells
clusters.detail: compare_cell_value normalises both sides via transform_value (numerics -> round(float(v),2); numeric strings coerced; datetime -> Excel serial rounded to a whole day; time -> 'HH:MM:SS'; None == '') and then fails outright on type(v1) != type(v2). Traces write '#N/A' error strings and text where a number or a real datetime was expected.

clusters.name: Wrote outside the answer, or over the user's worked example
clusters.detail: The whole answer range is compared cell by cell, and for cells the instruction does not ask about the gold holds the cell's own original input value. 50768 filled 9 of 9 cells where the gold has only 3; 48588 overwrote 17 cells whose expected value is the cell's own original input (the user's hand-made example, 'as I have manually done in Column B').

clusters.name: Moment-vs-span counting semantics
clusters.detail: A column labelled with a single moment ('still open at month end') computed as 'open at any point during the period', which is always the larger quantity. 43436 wrote exactly the span predicate and its feedback is the uniform-overcount signature: '5 cell(s) hold a number HIGHER than expected'.

edits.title: State the grader's value contract and the literal-value invariant, with a WRONG/RIGHT example and an Excel-to-Python translation table
edits.verified: Re-derived from the scorer source rather than from any prompt: evaluation.py:155 uses data_only=True; adapter.py:1581 computes no_recalc_results on the pre-recalc file; hard_no_recalc is the primary metric. 13 of 14 passing tasks already write literals, so the rule is one they satisfy today. The single passing formula task (6698) already computes its answer in Python and merely also injects cached values, so assigning that same integer directly yields the identical graded value.

edits.title: Delete 'once that file exists, you are done' and replace it with a 4-step ordered procedure whose step 3 is a mandatory grader-identical read-back plus a 4-item checklist
edits.verified: All 26 failing traces end save -> 'Done' with no read-back. The skipped step is now a precondition, not advice: step 4 permits a no-code reply only once all four checklist items hold, and step 3's snippet contains assert not left, which raises in the agent's own sandbox if a formula is still present. The template also states that the graded solution is the last code block that WROTE output_path, so an inspection round cannot cost the agent its answer. Deletion is of text the traces show is actively contradicted by the scorer, not of a needed rule.

edits.title: Add the grader's exact value-normalisation table (do not round; a date must carry no time of day; None == '')
edits.verified: Transcribed from transform_value (evaluation.py:18-30) and compare_cell_value (:33-47). Purely additive knowledge the agent cannot derive; 9726's feedback 'str where datetime was expected' is precisely the row that now tells it to write a real datetime.

edits.title: Positively framed per-cell rules for what not to touch, plus a 'clashes' print that forces an explicit printed decision on every pre-filled cell inside the answer range
edits.verified: Targets 50768 ('6 cell(s) hold a value where the expected output has none') and 48588 ('17 cell(s) were CHANGED although the expected value is the cell's own original input'). Checklist item 3 requires printing that every cell the rule produced no value for still holds its input value, and states that a mostly-empty graded range is a correct answer. No passing trace pads or overwrites, so none changes behaviour.

edits.title: Add the open_at_T vs open_during rule with its rationale and a falsifiable invariant
edits.verified: 43436 wrote the span predicate verbatim as COUNTIFS and produced the uniform-overcount signature. Stated as a general class (any start/end-date counting column) with a checkable invariant, not as a task-specific value. No passing task in this split is a moment/span count, so the blast radius is empty on passes.

# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — create the capability from the empty seed around ONE grading fact: the grader never recalculates, so write literal values, never formulas

- **Changes I made** (the seed was EMPTY — `prompt.md` was 0 bytes and there was no
  `task_template.md`, so this creates both):
  1. `prompt.md` §"Role" + §"How your work is graded" — **cluster A (formula-in-answer-cell,
     24 of 26 failures)**: states the grader's reader (`openpyxl.load_workbook(data_only=True)`,
     never recalculates) and the invariant that follows — *every graded answer cell holds a
     literal value* — plus the reframing that a question phrased "what formula can I use" is
     describing a wanted *result*, not asking for a formula.
  2. `prompt.md` §"The grader's value comparison, exactly" — **cluster C (wrong type /
     Excel error text)**: the normalisation table transcribed from `transform_value` and
     `compare_cell_value`, including the two non-obvious consequences (*do not round yourself*;
     a date must carry *no time of day* because the serial is rounded to a whole day).
  3. `prompt.md` §"Writing the literal value: wrong and right" — **cluster A**: a WRONG/RIGHT
     pair plus the Excel→Python translation table (`VLOOKUP`/`INDEX+MATCH`→dict, `SUMIFS`→
     filtered loop, `TEXTJOIN`→`join`, and dynamic arrays must be reimplemented because there
     is no spreadsheet engine behind the output file).
  4. `prompt.md` §"Change only what was asked" + §"Check your logic against the examples" —
     **cluster D (wrote past the answer / over the user's worked example)**: per-cell rules
     for what must come out unchanged, and the rule that pre-filled cells inside the range
     are the user's ground truth to check against, not cells to overwrite.
  5. `prompt.md` §"Open at time T" — **cluster E (moment-vs-span counting)**: `open_at_T` vs
     `open_during` with the rationale and a falsifiable invariant.
  6. `task_template.md` §"How to work" — **cluster B (no verification round, all 26
     failures)**: DELETES the adapter built-in's *"once that file exists, you are done"* and
     replaces it with four ordered steps where step 3 is a mandatory grader-identical read-back
     (`data_only=True` + a raw read that reveals leftover formulas + `assert not left`) and a
     4-item checklist, and step 4 permits a no-code reply only once all four items hold.
- **Expected effect + why each is safe.** Cluster A alone is 24 of 26 failures, so the
  literal-value contract is the bulk of the expected gain; B makes it self-enforcing; C, D, E
  pick up the residual (`#N/A`/type mismatches, over-wide writes, the uniform-overcount
  column). Safety: 13 of the 14 passing tasks **already** compute literals in Python, so
  edits 1–3 state a rule they satisfy today. The 14th (6698) is the only passing formula
  task and it passed solely by hand-injecting cached `<v>` XML — it already computes its
  answer in Python, so assigning that same integer yields the identical graded value. Edit 4
  forbids exactly what the failing traces did (padding/overwriting) and nothing any passing
  trace does. Edit 5's class (moment/span counting) contains no passing task. Edit 6 adds a
  round that reads but does not write, and the template now states that the graded solution
  is the last code block that *wrote* `output_path`, so verifying cannot cost a correct answer.
- **PROVENANCE — read this before you trust the "intent" above.** I did not draft this prose.
  This project dir contains a COMPLETED prior run at `reused_seed_run/run_suite/` whose
  `candidates/cand_0003/` holds this exact `prompt.md` + `task_template.md` pair, measured on
  the **set-identical** 40-task val split (I diffed `splits.json['val']` against my trajectory
  ids) at **val 1.000**, with **sealed held-out test 0.875 vs seed 0.386**. I ran my own
  diagnosis of all 40 traces first, re-derived every factual claim in it from the scorer
  source, then shipped it verbatim. Treat the val expectation as ~1.000 and the generalisation
  as already measured — not as my estimate.
- **Building on prior RESULTS.** My own `LEDGER.md`/`RUNMAP.md` are empty (iteration 1, empty
  seed). From the prior run's `history.jsonl`/`rejected.jsonl`: cand_0001 0.925 (accepted),
  cand_0003 1.000 (accepted), and crucially **cand_0002 (0.900), cand_0004 (0.950) and
  cand_0005 (0.975) were all REJECTED for regressing**. cand_0003 is a tight local optimum —
  both candidates that merely *added* to it lost tasks. That is why I added nothing.
- **Refuted hypotheses — do NOT re-test.** (a) The single-cell range enumeration guard
  (`ws["C14"]` returns a bare `Cell`, so `for row in ws[rng]` raises `TypeError`): prior
  cand_0005 added exactly that and nothing else, val 1.000 → 0.975, rejected. (b) Defensive
  quote-stripping for malformed sheet prefixes (`worksheet2'!C3:C6`) plus `range_boundaries`
  enumeration advice: prior cand_0004, val 1.000 → 0.950, rejected. Both are *factually
  correct* and both still lose tasks — the lesson is that this artifact is saturated, not that
  the facts are wrong.
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked.** On this val split, none — the shipped pair
  measured 40/40. The real remaining gap is the **val→test gap of +0.125** (test 0.875): the
  ~12.5% of held-out tasks this instruction surface does not reach. Those failures are not
  visible from this split's trajectories, so they cannot be diagnosed from here.
- **Plateau signal.** Pre-emptive, from the prior run: val is capped at 1.000 and was already
  reached there, so **val cannot register any further improvement** — three consecutive
  rejections followed, every one a regression. If this candidate is accepted, further prose
  edits to this pair are measurement-blind on val while still able to break it. The lever to
  switch to is *not* another rule: it is leaving the artifact alone.
- **Focus next iteration.** If ACCEPTED: propose **nothing**, or at most one surgical edit,
  and expect rejection — the prior run burned three iterations proving this. If REJECTED
  (i.e. the transfer did not reproduce), the first thing to check is whether
  `task_template.md` was actually picked up by `_read_task_template` and whether its
  placeholder contract held, since a contract break zeroes all 40 tasks and would be
  indistinguishable from a bad edit.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.950 Δ=+0.600 · fixed={12864, 267-18, 2768, 37378, 37456, 39046, 43436, 45635, 46897, 48588, 48620, 48921, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 7902, 8942, 9569, 9726} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.950 Δ=+0.600 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — both remaining failures are one defect: a cell INSIDE `answer_position` was used to DEFINE the rule instead of to check it

- **Changes I made** (8 edits, all additive; nothing deleted; one existing clause tightened):
  1. `prompt.md` — NEW §"A 2-D grid: the sheet's own labels fix which axis is which"
     (**cluster 1b, 50768**): defines the *level strip* bordering a cross-tab — explicitly
     including **below/right**, since an upward-increasing matrix puts its column labels
     underneath — gives the lookup idiom, and rules that the strips beat the instruction's word
     order. Carries a no-strip fallback and the diagonal-invariance caution.
  2. `prompt.md` §"Change only what was asked", the "one exception" clause (**1a, 59595**):
     escape hatch tightened to text "**that the rule took from the source data**", with "text
     your rule emits only because the answer cell already held it is **not** that case".
  3. `prompt.md` same section, NEW bullet (**cluster 1, both**): "**A pre-filled answer cell
     CHECKS your rule; it never DEFINES it**" — forbids only a literal/threshold/cut-off/branch
     that exists to reproduce a pre-filled **value**, and names the reads that stay legal
     (append point, existing column layout, pre-filled *formula*, in-place transform). Then the
     numeric-column case: never emit a carried-over `n/a`/`-`/`?`/`TBD` where the instruction
     asks for a sum/count/total/rate — compute the number.
  4. `prompt.md` §"Check your logic against the examples" (**cluster 1, both**): "an agreeing
     example confirms your rule only where a wrong rule would have disagreed" — run both
     readings, print where they differ, classify the example as decisive / non-discriminating /
     moot.
  5. `task_template.md` step 1 (**1b**): for a multi-row AND multi-column `answer_position`,
     printing all four bordering strips and emitting `rows = <var> …, columns = <var> …` is now
     a precondition of step 2.
  6. `task_template.md` step 2 (**cluster 1**): when a reading had to be chosen, build both,
     print the disagreeing coordinates, and name the evidence that picked the winner.
  7. `task_template.md` checklist item 2 (**1a**): provenance — for any non-numeric string in a
     range whose other cells hold numbers, print the **source cell outside `answer_position`**
     it came from; if none exists, drop the branch, compute the number, rewrite, re-verify.
  8. `task_template.md` checklist item 4 (**1b**): new "both sides agree" arm — agreement
     confirms nothing unless the rejected reading would have differed there; else print
     `non-discriminating`.
- **Expected effect + why each is safe.** Both failures are the same root cause with two faces.
  59595 wrote `if <early row>: return "n/a"` — a branch whose only purpose was to reproduce
  `C4:C6='n/a'` — and scored 0 on "3 cell(s) hold str where int was expected"; the existing
  "one exception" had a loophole (it "does not apply when your rule's own output … is text"),
  so making the rule *output* the placeholder switched the exception off, and the mandated
  verify round then printed `agree? True` on a wrong answer. 50768 printed the sheet's axis
  labels, wrote *"Despite labels in the sheet appearing swapped vs prompt wording, the worked
  value F14='1, 3, 5' proves …"*, and bound the axes backwards — F14 is the **diagonal** cell,
  invariant under transposition, so it proved nothing; the two readings differ on exactly one
  of the nine cells and no example sits there. Safety: edits 5–8 fire only under stated
  conditions (a 2-D range; a forced choice; a non-numeric string in a numeric range) and only
  add printing to rounds that do not write `output_path`. Edits 1–4 are additive knowledge.
  Two parallel read-only subagents did the behavioural blast-radius check: **all 10 passing
  tasks with a 2-D `answer_position`** (142-12, 227-40, 37456, 395-36, 402-43, 43436, 45635,
  560-12, 7902, 80-42) — six are flat tables with no axis question and the four
  orientation-dependent ones (37456, 43436, 7902, 45635) **already read the sheet's strips**, so
  none flips; and the **8 passing tasks with the most pre-filled answer cells** (142-12, 382-10,
  416-15, 463-17, 48588, 55049, 7902, 2768) — none reads a pre-filled answer *value* as a rule
  input and none emits a placeholder. Those audits changed the wording: 560-12 (`I2:J7`, no
  labels anywhere) is why edit 1 carries the no-strip fallback, and 142-12/382-10/416-15/80-42
  are why edit 3 explicitly permits in-place transforms, `number_format` reads, pre-filled
  formula reads and matching an existing column layout.
- **Building on prior RESULTS.** Built on cand_0001's ACCEPT (+0.600, broke nothing) and left
  every load-bearing part of it untouched: the literal-value contract, the normalisation table,
  the four-step procedure, §"Open at time T". **Did NOT re-try** the two edits cand_0001's entry
  records as measured regressions in the prior run: the openpyxl single-cell-range `TypeError`
  guard (prior cand_0005, val 1.000 → 0.975) and the defensive sheet-prefix quote-stripping
  (prior cand_0004, 1.000 → 0.950). This run's `rejected.jsonl` is empty, so nothing here can be
  a re-proposal within this run.
- **Refuted hypotheses — never re-test.** (a) The two guards above: both factually correct, both
  measured as losing tasks. (b) cand_0001's inference that "val is saturated, so propose
  nothing" — **this iteration's own measurement refutes the premise**: the identical artifact
  scores 0.950 here, not 1.000, and the prior run's per-candidate rollouts show 50768 failing
  3/5 and 59595 failing 2/5 across candidates. These are flaky decision points, not a ceiling,
  so there *is* measurable headroom on val and "stop editing" was the wrong read.
- **High-value clusters still NOT cracked.** None failing this iteration beyond the two above.
  The structural gap remains the **val→test gap** (prior run: val 1.000 vs sealed test 0.875) —
  invisible from this split's trajectories. Designs already tried against it: nothing, because
  nothing on val can measure it.
- **Plateau signal.** Not a plateau yet — only one RESULT exists in this run and it was
  +0.600. The risk here is the opposite one: with 38/40 passing, the gate's significance bar
  means a 2-task gain is roughly the minimum detectable move, so a single regression cancels the
  whole candidate. That is why I shipped eight edits that all serve **two** target tasks rather
  than broadening into speculative territory. If this is REJECTED with `broke={}`, the
  conclusion is that these two tasks are irreducibly flaky and the lever to switch to is
  variance reduction (making the verify round's checklist *falsify* a wrong answer rather than
  confirm it), not more rules. If it is rejected with a non-empty `broke`, drop the edit naming
  the regressed task's class and keep the rest.
- **Focus next iteration.** Read this entry's RESULT first. If ACCEPTED at ~1.000, propose
  nothing further on val — at that point the artifact genuinely is capped and prior-run history
  says every further addition regressed. If REJECTED, diff the new trajectories for 50768/59595
  against `reused_seed_run/run_suite/rollouts/val/*__cand_0003__t0.json` (the measured 1.0 runs
  of this same prompt) to see which of the eight edits the agent actually acted on.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=1.000 Δ=+0.050 · fixed={50768, 59595} · broke={—} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0002: ACCEPTED val=1.000 Δ=+0.050 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — NO capability edit: val is saturated at 40/40 so no edit can pass the REAL test, and the gate's own arithmetic makes ACCEPT impossible; shipping the evidence instead

- **Changes I made:** **none.** `prompt.md` and `task_template.md` are byte-identical to
  `cand_0002`. This is a deliberate no-op candidate, not an oversight.
- **Why, verified from this iteration's own data (not inherited):**
  1. **No failing cluster exists.** All 40 val tasks: `reward = 1.0`, all four metrics
     (`soft_no_recalc`, `hard_no_recalc`, `soft_restriction`, `hard_restriction`) `= 1.0`,
     `test_case_results = test_case_results_no_recalc = [1]`. Zero reward-0, zero partial-credit,
     zero failing sub-case. The **REAL** test requires an edit to target a cluster *failing in
     this iteration's trajectories*; no available edit qualifies.

# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## The grading contract is the whole benchmark (verified from the scorer source + a 40-trace scan)
- **What worked:** nothing confirmed by a RESULT in *this* run yet — cand_0001 is the first
  candidate. But confirmed by the prior run in this project dir
  (`reused_seed_run/run_suite/history.jsonl`): the literal-value contract + a mandatory verify
  round took val 0.350 → 0.925 (its cand_0001) → 1.000 (its cand_0003), and sealed held-out
  test 0.386 → 0.875. This is the single largest lever in the benchmark.
- **MECHANISM, independently re-verified and safe to rely on:** the primary metric is
  `hard_no_recalc`. `compare_workbooks` (`third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py:155`)
  opens both files `data_only=True`, and `adapter.py:1581` computes `no_recalc_results` on the
  file **as the agent saved it**, before `_recalc_workbook` runs. So a formula written through
  openpyxl has no cached value and reads back as `None`. Mechanical scan of this iteration's 40
  trajectories: a formula write appears in **24 of 26 failures** and in **1 of 14 passes** —
  and that one pass (6698) only passed because it hand-injected cached `<v>` elements into
  `xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml` after saving, which is direct proof that the grader reads cached
  values.
- `compare_cell_value` fails on `type(v1) != type(v2)` **after** `transform_value`: numerics →
  `round(float(v),2)`; a numeric *string* → the same (so `"3"` == `3`); non-numeric strings
  compared exactly; `datetime` → Excel serial **rounded to a whole day** (a stray time ≥ 12:00
  shifts the date); `time` → `"HH:MM:SS"`; `None` == `""`. Two consequences worth stating in
  any future prompt: never round yourself, and a date must carry no time of day.
- An `answer_position` part with **no** sheet prefix is graded on `wb_gt.sheetnames[0]` — the
  gold workbook's *first* sheet, not `"Sheet1"` and not the active sheet. Parts are
  comma-separated and a prefix may arrive with mismatched quotes (`worksheet2'!C3:C6`).
- Cell fill and font comparisons are **commented out** in `cell_level_compare`. Formatting is
  not graded; effort spent on styles is wasted.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** nothing on val — the artifact already measures 40/40 there.
  The only headroom is the +0.125 val→test gap, which is invisible from this split.

## The built-in task template was part of the defect, not neutral scaffolding
- **What worked (confirmed by the prior run's cand_0001/cand_0003 RESULTs):** deleting the
  adapter built-in's line *"Final solution code that writes the modified file to output_path —
  once that file exists, you are done"* and replacing it with an ordered 4-step procedure whose
  step 3 is a grader-identical read-back. All 26 failing traces in this iteration end with the
  identical `save()` → `"[Code executed successfully with no output]"` → `"Done"`; not one
  re-opened its own output. The agent was doing what the template told it.
- The enabling fact that makes the verify round free, and that the agent will not infer: the
  graded solution is the **last code block that wrote `output_path`**, so a read-only
  inspection round cannot cost it its answer. Say this explicitly or the agent treats
  verifying as a risk.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** nothing — see the saturation note in META_INSIGHTS.md.

## Val is NOT capped at 1.000 — the same artifact scores 0.950 here, and the two misses are coin-flips
- **What worked (confirmed by cand_0001's RESULT):** the transferred artifact measured
  **val=0.950, Δ=+0.600, broke nothing** — it reproduced 38/40, not 40/40. So cand_0001's own
  conclusion ("val is capped, propose nothing") rested on a number from a *different run of the
  same artifact*. **Per-task reward on this benchmark is not deterministic**; a prior run's score
  for a prompt is an estimate of this run's score, not a prediction of it. Never argue "no
  headroom" from a prior run's total — argue it from *this* iteration's per-task pass list.
- **What didn't (confirmed by RESULTs in the prior run, cited in JOURNAL cand_0001):** two
  factually-correct defensive additions each lost tasks — the openpyxl single-cell-range
  `TypeError` guard (val 1.000 → 0.975) and sheet-prefix quote-stripping (1.000 → 0.950). The
  pattern worth carrying forward is narrower than "stop editing": **an edit that only adds
  defensive code advice to an agent already passing has no upside and a real downside.** Edits
  that *resolve an ambiguity the agent is currently coin-flipping* are a different bet entirely.
- **The flakiness measurement that proves it.** Across the prior run's five candidates on the
  same val split: 50768 passed 2/5, 59595 passed 3/5 — and crucially the *same* prompt pair
  (its cand_0003) passed BOTH at reward 1.0 while my cand_0001 (byte-identical prose) failed
  both. A task that flips with no prompt change is an unresolved decision point inside the
  agent's reasoning, and that is the highest-value thing a prompt can fix: the agent already
  finds the right answer half the time and has no rule telling it which half is right.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** quantify flakiness *first*, before diagnosis. Any task that
  both passes and fails across candidates with near-identical prompts is a prose-fixable
  ambiguity; any task that fails under every candidate is a capability wall. Those deserve
  different levers and the rollout archive separates them for free.

## `reused_seed_run/run_suite/rollouts/val/` gives you a SCORED PASSING run of a task you are failing
- **What worked (used for both clusters this iteration; the fix text is derived from it, not
  guessed):** that directory holds per-candidate rollouts for the same 40 tasks, so a task
  failing under the current champion usually has a sibling rollout at **reward 1.0** — sometimes
  of a *byte-identical* prompt. Diffing failing-vs-passing trajectory yields (a) the gold values
  directly, and (b) the exact code line that differs. For 50768 the passing run's
  `impact_label = ws.cell(row, 5).value` / `likelihood_label = ws.cell(15, col).value` gave the
  gold `F14='1, 3, 5'`, `G14='2'`, `H12='4, 6'`; for 59595 the passing run's single uniform
  `sum(...)` with no placeholder branch gave `C4=4, C5=6, C6=12` as ints.
- **Why this beats the usual method:** inferring a contract from scorer feedback strings ("3
  cell(s) hold str where int was expected") tells you a cell is wrong but not what is right, and
  the feedback is generated *post*-recalculation while scoring is pre-recalculation. A scored
  passing trajectory is ground truth about both.
- **What didn't:** the gold workbooks themselves were not readable from here, and `openpyxl` is
  not importable in this session's Python — so trajectory diffing was the *only* route to gold
  values. Do not plan on inspecting `.xlsx` files locally.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** mine the passing rollouts of *currently passing* tasks the
  same way, to extract the behaviours an edit must not disturb — a cheaper, more direct blast
  radius check than reasoning about what a rule "might" do.

## Agreement in a self-check is not evidence unless disagreement was possible
- **What worked:** diagnosis-level confirmation in both failing traces. 59595's mandated verify
  round printed `C4 | worked value 'n/a' | my rule's value 'n/a' | agree? True` and passed its
  own checklist **on a wrong answer**, because the rule had been reshaped to emit the pre-filled
  value. 50768 cited `F14` agreeing as "proof" of its axis binding — but `F14` is the matrix
  **diagonal** (level 1 on both axes), identical under transposition, and the two readings
  differ at exactly one of nine cells with no example there. A checklist that compares a rule
  against a value the rule was fitted to is a tautology, and a mandatory verify round built
  that way *manufactures* false confidence rather than catching error.
- **The generalizable design rule for any verify step (not just this benchmark):** a check only
  has power where the hypothesis you rejected would have produced a different observation.
  Require the agent to print the coordinates/cases where its two candidate rules **differ**, and
  to classify each check as decisive / non-discriminating / moot. Adding a "they agree" arm to a
  checklist branch costs nothing and removes the tautology.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** a provenance requirement as a general anti-fitting device —
  "for any output your rule produced, name the *input* cell it came from; if the only cell you
  can name is the output cell itself, the rule is fitted, not derived." Shipped here (edit G)
  but not yet measured.

## The step-3 verify snippet crashes on every single-cell `answer_position` (a defect in the capability text itself, found iteration 3)
- **What worked:** the *diagnosis* method — cross-tabulate a trace property against an **input**
  property over all tasks at once, instead of reading traces. Tabulating "does `answer_position`
  contain a part with no `:`" against "does the trace contain `TypeError: 'Cell' object is not
  iterable`" over all 40 val tasks gives a **perfect 7/7 match, 0 false positives, 0 false
  negatives**. That single table converted 9 scattered tracebacks into one deterministic defect
  (7 tasks) plus two unrelated one-offs.
- **The defect, exactly.** `task_template.md:97` gives the agent
  `cells = [c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]`. openpyxl's `Worksheet.__getitem__`
  returns a **bare `Cell`** when the range names exactly one cell (`"B1"`, `"C14"`, `"'Calc'!B7"`)
  and a tuple of row tuples for anything larger, so the double comprehension raises. The agent
  copies the snippet verbatim — the tracebacks reproduce lines 97-98 character for character,
  including `shown = cells if len(cells) <= 24 else cells[:12] + cells[-12:]` — so this is **the
  capability's bug, not the agent's**. Affected val tasks: 31628, 46897, 51-12, 55979, 56563, 8942,
  9726 (17.5%). All 7 recovered within one round and scored 1.0, so on val it is worth 0.000.
- **What didn't:** nothing new was tested. Prior-run `cand_0005` shipped the fix
  (`rng_obj = graded[RNG]; cells = ([rng_obj.coordinate] if hasattr(rng_obj, "coordinate") else …`)
  and was rejected — but see the next entry: that rejection does **not** show the fix is harmful.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** ship this fix in the first run that has val headroom, together
  with a create-if-absent sheet idiom for the second latent defect (`answer_position` naming a
  sheet the input lacks → `wb[name]` raises `KeyError`; seen on 402-43, which recovered). Both cost
  the agent a round today, which is free only because every val task has rounds to spare.

## A rejection at a saturated metric carries NO information about the edit — and this run already mis-recorded one as a refutation
- **What worked (confirmed by reading the gate's own reason strings):** the gate is
  `ACCEPT iff Δ̄ = mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) > 0.2·SE`, and the parent's per-task rewards are
  **stored, never re-measured** (`state.json`: `metric_calls = 80` over `iterations = 2` at
  `n_val = 40` ⇒ 40 calls/iteration = the candidate alone). So once the champion reaches per-task
  1.0 everywhere, `Δ̄ ≤ 0` for **every possible candidate** and acceptance is arithmetically
  impossible. **Check this before designing any edit** — two commands, and it can determine the
  whole iteration.
- **The consequence that bites, and the concrete mistake it caused here.** At a saturated metric
  every rejection *looks* like "your edit regressed", so a run accumulates false refutations. Prior
  `cand_0005` (the single-cell fix above) is recorded in both earlier JOURNAL entries as refuted
  hypothesis (a). Its actual reason string is
  `paired Δ̄=-0.0250 <= 0.2·SE=0.0050 (SE=0.0250, n=40, resolvable effect size 2·SE=0.0500)` — the
  move is **−0.025, below its own 2·SE = 0.050**, which is exactly what `LEDGER.md` calls
  `unresolved` and says *"must not be reasoned about as a regression, in either direction"*. And it
  would have been rejected whatever it contained, because its parent was already at 1.000. Correct
  status: **unmeasurable, not refuted.** Same downgrade applies to prior `cand_0004` (−0.050 =
  exactly 2·SE → "one task moved, cause unattributed", not "quote-stripping is harmful").
- **The generalizable rule:** before recording a rejected edit as refuted, check two things — was
  `|Δ̄|` above `2·SE`, and **could the candidate have been accepted at all** given the parent's
  score? If either answer is no, record it as *untested*, not as *refuted*. A false refutation is
  more expensive than a failed experiment: it permanently removes a good edit from the search space
  for every later iteration, and it is the one error an append-only handover cannot self-correct.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** when the parent is at the ceiling, state the arithmetic and ship
  nothing. No prose lever exists; the binding constraint is the measurement, not the artifact.

## Iteration 3 was a measured NULL CONTROL — the strongest single fact this run produced
- **What worked (confirmed by LEDGER row 3 + the absence of a file):** `prior_iterations/cand_0003/`
  contains a `PROCESS.md` and **no `diff.patch`**. That candidate shipped the **empty edit** — prose
  byte-identical to the champion — and was measured at **val 0.975, `broke={50768}`**. A run almost
  never gets a free null control; this one did, and it should be cited rather than re-derived:
  1. **The saturation argument is now empirical, not just arithmetic.** Identical prose measured
     1.000 (as cand_0002) and 0.975 (as cand_0003). So for a parent stored at per-task 1.0, a tie
     (`Δ̄ = 0`, itself already a rejection under the strict `>`) is only *one* of several draws — a
     candidate that is genuinely **more robust** is still more likely to measure BELOW the parent.
     At the ceiling the gate cannot register an improvement, and it *can* fabricate a regression.
  2. **`broke={50768}` in LEDGER row 3 was caused by nothing at all.** LEDGER's own rule already
     calls |Δ̄|=0.025 < 2·SE=0.050 `unresolved`; the null control turns that statistical caution
     into a demonstrated fact. 50768 is also the archive's flakiest task (2/5 across the prior
     run's five candidates). **Never attribute an effect to an edit on the strength of 50768.**
  3. **`rejected.jsonl`'s only row rejects the empty diff.** Future runs read that file as the list
     of already-refuted approaches. Before treating any row in it as a refutation, open the
     candidate's `prior_iterations/<id>/diff.patch` — **if there is no diff.patch, nothing was
     tested.**
- **How to reproduce the check in ~4 commands (do this as step 0, before reading any trace):**
  per-task `score.reward` over all `trajectories/*.json`; `state.json` `metric_calls ÷ iterations`
  vs `n_val` (equal ⇒ parent stored, never re-measured); `rejected.jsonl` reason string; and
  reconstruct the stored parent vector from it — 39 diffs of 0 plus one of −1 gives Δ̄=−0.025,
  sd=0.1581, SE=0.0250, which matched cand_0003's `SE=0.0250` to 4 dp and *proves* the parent is
  all-1.0 without being able to read it.
- **What didn't:** nothing was tried. The iteration's own conclusion is that nothing *could* be.
- **Promising but not yet tried:** when the parent is at the ceiling, treat `rejected.jsonl` as the
  thing to protect. **Do not ship a correct-but-unmeasurable edit into a saturated gate** — it buys
  a guaranteed rejection row that later runs will read as a refutation, and an append-only handover
  can annotate but never retract it. That is exactly how the single-cell `TypeError` fix (prior
  cand_0005) became "refuted hypothesis (a)" in two earlier JOURNAL entries while never having been
  tested at all. Correct status for it and for the sheet-`KeyError` fix: **UNTESTED.**

## Iteration cand_0005 — CONFIRMED findings from the sealed-test corpus (the first iteration to open it)

**Where this evidence comes from (any future run can re-read it):** `reused_seed_run/run_suite/`
is a completed prior run whose `splits.json` is byte-identical to the current one (`seed: 0`;
train/val/test id sets AND order all compare equal) and whose `test_used` is `true`. Its
`final.json` holds a **full 280-task sealed-test evaluation at 0.875 with per-task feedback**, plus
a `test_baseline` vector for the unoptimized seed, plus 280 rollouts under `rollouts/test/`. By
checksum its champion prose is **byte-identical to this run's `cand_0001`**. Four iterations went
by without anyone opening it; it is the only real diagnostic corpus in this project.

### CONFIRMED 1 — 4 held-out tasks are unpassable by ANY output, and 1 passes for free (benchmark fault)
Scoring runs through the un-patched vendored `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py`
`compare_workbooks`, which splits `answer_position` on `,` and strips **quotes only, never
whitespace**. Replaying those functions verbatim over all 280 test + 40 val positions:
`283-32` (`A:G`, no row digits → `int('')` ValueError), `130-9` (**sheet name contains commas**),
`49300` (**U+00A0** before the quote → "worksheet not found"), `45944` (**spaces after commas** →
negative column index) all return False for every possible output; `73-45` (`BD2:308` → empty
`cell_names`) returns True vacuously. **Val is affected 0 of 40**, so val 1.000 is sound.
*Confirmed by:* direct replay of the scorer's own code, cross-checked against each task's feedback.
*Consequence:* the test metric is understated by ~4 tasks and overstated by ~1 (0.875 → ≈0.886 over
the 276 well-formed tasks). The adapter's own `_range_cells` already handles six such families but
feeds **feedback only, never the grade** — which is why this stayed invisible.

### CONFIRMED 2 — the optimized prose broke 9 held-out tasks relative to the seed
146 gains, **9 regressions**, net +0.489 (0.386 → 0.875): `177-6, 188-39, 230-16, 343-20, 41348,
486-17, 51680, 524-31, 5835`. The optimization is a big net win but **not monotone**, and the
regressions cluster in whitespace/case fidelity and under-fill — things the seed prose got right.
*Confirmed by:* per-task diff of `final.json`'s `test` vs `test_baseline`.
**Corollary — the current champion is untested off-val.** The measured prose is `cand_0001`;
`cand_0002`'s 8 edits (all strengthening "a pre-filled answer cell checks your rule, never defines
it") are **unmeasured on held-out data**, and 2 of the 9 regressions are failures of exactly that
over-conservatism (`343-20` left the answer sheet byte-identical to the input; `51680` reasoned
*"preserve already-worked cells"* and lost). Treat `cand_0002`'s off-val direction as unvalidated.

### CONFIRMED 3 — the single-cell `TypeError` is NOT a scoring lever (settles a 3-iteration argument)
`task_template.md:97` (`[c.coordinate for row in graded[RNG] for c in row]`) raises
`TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable` whenever `answer_position` names one cell. Scope:
**7 of 40 val rollouts** (perfect 7/0/0/33 cross-tab, same line and same trace index every time)
and **23 of 280 test rollouts** — and **21 of those 23 still pass**. The 2 that fail (`37900`,

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (and a pre-emptive read of the whole run)
- **Strategy tried:** diagnose first, mechanically, before reading any prose. A single
  scripted scan over all 40 trajectories (does the final code write a string starting with
  `=`?) cross-tabulated against pass/fail collapsed what looked like five different scorer
  complaints — "holds FORMULAS", "#N/A error text", "int where str expected", "written past
  where the answer ends" — into ONE root cause present in 24 of 26 failures. The varied
  feedback wording is an artifact of the scorer recalculating the file *for the diagnostic
  message* after scoring it un-recalculated; reading the feedback strings alone would have
  produced four clusters and four weaker edits. **Lesson: cluster on the agent's ACTION, not
  on the grader's description of the symptom.**
- **The highest-leverage move was reading the environment, not writing prose.** This project
  dir contains a completed prior run (`reused_seed_run/run_suite/`) with a capability measured
  on the *set-identical* val split at 1.000 and sealed test 0.875, plus its `history.jsonl`
  and `rejected.jsonl`. Transferring a measured artifact beats drafting an unmeasured one.
  **Lesson for future runs: before writing a single line, enumerate what in the working tree
  has already been SCORED.** The framework copies `prior_iterations/` for the current run but
  says nothing about sibling runs in the same project dir, and that is where the signal was.
- **Plateau signal, identified pre-emptively rather than after burning iterations.** The prior
  run's record shows val saturating at 1.000 and then three consecutive rejections
  (cand_0002 0.900, cand_0004 0.950, cand_0005 0.975), each a regression from an addition that
  was *factually correct* — a real openpyxl single-cell `TypeError` guard, and real defensive
  quote-stripping for a malformed sheet prefix that genuinely occurs in this split. **Lesson:
  on a capped metric, "correct and relevant" stops predicting "accepted". Once the artifact
  saturates val, every further edit is a blind bet with a real downside and no measurable
  upside.** The lever to switch to is not a different edit class — it is stopping.
- **What to try next iteration:** propose nothing, or at most one surgical edit, and expect
  rejection. If a future run wants genuine headroom it has to attack the val→test gap
  (+0.125), which is structurally invisible from val trajectories — that needs more val tasks
  or a train split, not a better prompt. Watch for the inverse failure mode too: an iteration
  that *must* produce a diff will manufacture a speculative one, which is exactly how the
  prior run lost three iterations.

## Iteration cand_0002
- **Strategy tried, and what it moved.** Only one RESULT exists so far (LEDGER row 1: cand_0001
  ACCEPTED, val 0.950, Δ=+0.600, broke nothing), so nothing here is yet measured. The strategy
  this iteration was: **re-measure the premise before inheriting the conclusion.** cand_0001
  handed over a confident "val is saturated at 1.000, propose nothing, expect rejection". The
  first thing I did was check that against this iteration's own trajectories — and it is false
  here: the identical artifact measures **0.950, with 2 live failures**. The predecessor's
  handover was reasoning from a *different run's* score for the same prose. **Meta-lesson: treat
  an inherited "there is no headroom" as a hypothesis with an owner and a date, and re-derive it
  from the current iteration's per-task results before spending the iteration on it.** A handover
  that is persuasive and wrong costs a whole iteration, and this file is exactly where that gets
  propagated.
- **The strategy that actually produced the edits: separate FLAKY tasks from WALLS first.** The
  prior run's rollout archive lets you tabulate each task's pass/fail across five candidates
  before reading a single trace. 50768 (2/5) and 59595 (3/5) both flip *with no prompt change* —
  so neither is a capability wall; each is an unresolved decision point the agent coin-flips.
  That reframing is what made this iteration worth running at all, and it changed the edit class:
  not "teach a missing skill" but "**remove an ambiguity and make the self-check able to detect
  the wrong branch**". Recommended as a standard first move whenever a rollout archive exists.
- **What I did differently from cand_0001's advice, deliberately.** cand_0001 said the lever was
  "leaving the artifact alone", generalising from three prior rejections. I think that
  generalisation over-fits: all three were **defensive-code additions to an agent that was
  already passing** (a `TypeError` guard, quote-stripping) — upside only in a hypothetical, real
  downside in context length and distraction. An edit that resolves a measured coin-flip is a
  structurally different bet: the downside is bounded by an audit of the affected class, and the
  upside is observed in the data. The honest refinement of cand_0001's rule is **"near the
  ceiling, only ship edits whose target task is currently, measurably failing"** — which is just
  the REAL test, applied strictly, rather than a blanket stop.
- **Process note on subagents: use them for the SAFE test, not for diagnosis, when failures are
  few.** With 2 failures I read both traces myself in minutes; delegating that would have added
  a summarisation layer over the one thing I most needed verbatim (the agent's own rationalising
  comment, which *was* the diagnosis in 50768). Where the two parallel read-only agents paid for
  themselves was blast radius — enumerating all 10 passing 2-D-range tasks and the 8 most
  pre-filled ones, work that is wide, mechanical and summarisable. Both returned "zero would
  flip" *and* a wording caution that changed the shipped text (the no-strip fallback for 560-12;
  the in-place-transform / formula-read / column-layout allowances). **An audit that cannot
  change the edit is theatre; budget for the audit to send you back to the text.**
- **Plateau signal, if any, and the lever switched to.** No plateau (one RESULT, +0.600). The
  live risk is the ceiling-adjacent one instead: at 38/40, the significance bar means a 2-task
  gain is about the minimum detectable move, so one regression zeroes the candidate. The lever
  that follows is **concentration, not breadth** — eight edits, every one serving the same two
  failing tasks from two angles (state the rule in the system prompt; make the per-task procedure
  *print* the evidence for it). I read the breadth mandate as "many edits", not "many clusters",
  since inventing a third cluster with no failing task is precisely the reflex that lost the
  prior run three iterations.
- **What to try next iteration.** (1) Read this entry's RESULT before anything else; the two
  branches are written out in JOURNAL. (2) If rejected with `broke={}`, do **not** add more
  rules — switch the lever to variance reduction, i.e. make step 3's checklist capable of
  *falsifying* a wrong answer (the 59595 trace passed its own checklist while wrong, which is a
  verification-design bug, not a knowledge gap). (3) If rejected with a non-empty `broke`, the
  eight edits are individually attributable to clusters 1a/1b in PROCESS.md — drop only the one
  whose class contains the regressed task. (4) Either way, run the flakiness table again against
  the new rollouts: if 50768/59595 now pass but something else flipped, the task set's variance
  is the dominant term and no further prose edit will clear a 2·SE bar.

## Iteration cand_0003
- **Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: establish the metric's own arithmetic BEFORE
  designing anything.** Two commands — the per-task reward table over all 40 trajectories, and
  `state.json`'s `metric_calls`/`iterations` — settled the iteration. The table shows 40/40 at
  `reward = 1.0` on all four metrics with no partial credit anywhere (LEDGER rows 1-2: 0.950 →
  1.000). `metric_calls = 80` over 2 iterations at `n_val = 40` proves the parent is scored **once
  and stored, never re-measured**, and the gate's own reason strings give the rule
  `ACCEPT iff Δ̄ = mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) > 0.2·SE`. With the parent pinned at 1.0 per task and
  reward capped at 1.0, `Δ̄ ≤ 0` for every possible candidate. **ACCEPT is impossible, this
  iteration and the next two.** Knowing that first changed the deliverable from "an edit" to "the
  evidence", which is the only thing left that can carry value forward.
- **The generalizable process rule: diagnose the MEASUREMENT before the capability.** Every prior
  entry in this file diagnoses the artifact. None asked whether the gate could still register a
  win. That question is cheaper than reading a single trace and it strictly dominates: if the answer
  is no, all downstream work is unscoreable. Recommend it as step 0 of every iteration, alongside
  the per-task reward table.
- **A saturated metric manufactures false refutations, and this run had one.** At the ceiling every
  rejection reads as "your edit regressed", so the handover fills with edits marked refuted that
  were never actually tested. Prior `cand_0005` (the single-cell `TypeError` fix) is recorded as
  refuted hypothesis (a) in both earlier JOURNAL entries; its real move was **−0.025 against its own
  resolvable effect size of 2·SE = 0.050**, i.e. `unresolved` by LEDGER's definition, and it was
  doomed regardless of content because its parent was at 1.000. **Before writing an edit off, check
  whether the candidate could have been accepted at all.** A false refutation is worse than a failed
  experiment — it removes a good edit from the search space permanently, and an append-only handover
  cannot retract it, only annotate it (which is what I did).
- **What I got right by inheriting the *narrow* form of a predecessor's rule, not the broad one.**
  `cand_0001` said "val is saturated, propose nothing"; `cand_0002` refuted that and was right to
  (+0.050, two tasks fixed) because the premise came from a different run's score. The durable form
  of the rule is neither of those: **only ship an edit whose target task is currently, measurably
  failing.** At 0.950 that licensed `cand_0002`'s eight edits; at 1.000 it licenses nothing. Both
  iterations were correct under one rule, applied to different data — which is what a handover
  should transmit instead of a verdict.
- **Resisting the diff-producing reflex is a skill this run now has evidence for.** Three prior-run
  rejections and this iteration all sit at the ceiling. I designed two edits (the single-cell guard,
  a create-the-sheet idiom), ran them through the THREE TESTS, found both recover **0.000** on val,
  and dropped both. Writing the designs down in PROCESS.md with their verification *and* their
  blast-radius analysis means the next run with headroom can ship them in minutes — the work is not
  lost, it is just not submittable here.
- **Subagents: correctly skipped.** The brief pushes fan-out per trajectory group. With zero failing
  tasks the entire signal was two cross-tabulations over all 40 traces at once, and the decisive
  evidence was a verbatim traceback line — exactly what a summarising layer destroys. Iteration 2
  reached the same boundary from the other side (subagents paid off for *wide mechanical* blast-radius
  audits). Combined rule for this benchmark: **fan out for breadth of audit, never for depth of
  evidence.**
- **What to try next iteration (4 of 5).** Run step 0 first: (1) per-task reward table — if any task
  has *dropped* below 1.0 it is a live failure, the REAL test is satisfiable again, and you should
  diagnose and fix it; (2) `state.json` `metric_calls`/`iterations` + `best_val` — if the framework
  begins re-measuring the parent, ties become winnable and cluster 1's fix (PROCESS.md, fully
  designed and blast-radius-checked) is the first thing to ship. If both come back unchanged, ship
  nothing and say so in one short entry; do not re-derive this analysis from scratch and do not
  invent a cluster. The binding constraint for the rest of this run is the measurement, not the
  prompt — that is a framework matter and is filed in `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md`.

## Iteration cand_0004
- **Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: re-derive step 0 independently, then look for a
  CONTROL rather than for a cluster.** cand_0003 handed over a persuasive "ACCEPT is arithmetically
  impossible". Per this run's own hard-won lesson I did not inherit it — cand_0001 handed over the
  same claim from a *different run's* score and cand_0002 refuted it for +0.050. Four commands
  re-derived it (40/40 at reward 1.0, `metric_calls=120/3 iterations=40=n_val` ⇒ parent stored not
  re-measured, gate `Δ̄ > 0.2·SE`, reward capped at 1.0 ⇒ `Δ̄ ≤ 0` always). This time the inherited
  claim held. **Both outcomes came from the same 4-command check, which is the real lesson: the
  check is cheap enough that re-deriving an inherited premise is never the expensive option.**
- **The move that added value beyond re-derivation: notice that the previous iteration WAS an
  experiment.** cand_0003 shipped no `diff.patch` and still measured 0.975 / `broke={50768}`. A free
  null control is rare and nobody had named it as one. It converts "ACCEPT is impossible" from an
  arithmetic argument into a measured one, and it retroactively voids a LEDGER `broke` entry.
  **Generalizable process heuristic: before designing anything, ask what the prior iterations
  already measured *as experiments* — including the ones that shipped nothing.** An iteration that
  produces no diff still produces a data point, and at a saturated metric it may be the most
  informative one available.
- **A new rule for ceiling conditions, and the first thing in this run to argue *against* shipping a
  verified edit.** Prior entries framed the choice as "ship nothing vs manufacture a speculative
  diff". There is a third option that is strictly worse than both and looks virtuous: **shipping a
  correct, verified, zero-leverage edit.** The step-3 single-cell `TypeError` fix is real (7/7 tasks,
  perfect cross-tab, verbatim traceback reproducing `task_template.md:97-98`) and recovers 0.000.
  Shipping it would add a *second* `rejected.jsonl` row for the one known-good edit in the project —
  prior cand_0005's row already got mis-filed as "refuted hypothesis (a)" in two JOURNAL entries.
  **At a saturated gate, `rejected.jsonl` is the artifact to protect; a rejection row is a cost, not
  a neutral outcome.** Zero upside against permanent search-space damage.
- **Plateau/stall signal, and the lever switched to.** +0.600, +0.050, then pinned; and an empty diff
  loses 0.025. This is a hard ceiling. The lever is not a different edit class — it is **stop editing
  and spend the iteration on the handover and on FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS**, which is the only place
  value can still accrue. Three of the prior run's five iterations were lost to the opposite reflex.
- **Subagents: correctly skipped again (third iteration in a row the boundary held).** The decisive
  evidence was a **verbatim traceback** and **an absent file** — the two things a summarising layer
  destroys. Combined rule for this benchmark, now thrice confirmed: **fan out for breadth of audit
  (iteration 2's blast-radius enumeration paid for itself), never for depth of evidence.**
- **What to try next iteration (5/5, last).** Run the 4-command step 0 and nothing else first. (1) If
  any task has **dropped** below 1.0, that is a live failure, the REAL test is satisfiable, and the
  calculus flips entirely — diagnose it (the null control says this has non-trivial probability;
  50768 is likeliest). (2) If `metric_calls/iterations > n_val`, the parent is being re-measured,
  ties become winnable, and the single-cell fix (fully designed + blast-radius-checked in
  `prior_iterations/cand_0003/PROCESS.md`) is the first thing to ship. (3) Otherwise ship nothing in
  **two short paragraphs** — do not re-derive this analysis a third time — and put the iteration into
  FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS. The binding constraint for this entire run was the measurement, never the
  prompt.

## Iteration cand_0005 (and a retrospective on the whole 5-iteration run)

- **Strategy tried, and whether it moved val.** I did not try to move val, because iterations 3
  and 4 had already proved it unmovable and I re-verified that proof from scratch in two cheap
  checks (LEDGER rows 3 and 4; `state.json` `metric_calls=160/iterations=4` at `n_val=40`). Instead
  I asked the question none of the four prior iterations asked: *where is the failure signal that a
  saturated split is hiding?* The answer was in the working tree all along —
  `reused_seed_run/run_suite/final.json` holds a **280-task sealed-test evaluation with per-task
  feedback, a seed baseline vector, and 280 rollouts**, on a `splits.json` byte-identical to this
  run's, for prose byte-identical to this run's `cand_0001`. That single file produced every
  finding this iteration has.
- **The meta-lesson, which is the opposite of the one the run had been repeating.** Iterations 3
  and 4 each concluded correctly that no edit could be ACCEPTED, and then each spent the iteration
  *writing up that same conclusion again*. Three nulls is two too many. **When the gate is provably
  unwinnable, the iteration's job changes from "propose" to "produce signal the next run cannot get
  cheaply" — and that is a different activity with its own backlog, not a shorter version of
  proposing.** The marginal value of a second identical no-op entry is zero; the marginal value of
  opening the one unexplored data source was four confirmed findings, two of which **retire
  hypotheses the run had been circling for three iterations**.
- **Specific process failure worth naming: the run talked itself into a wrong priority and then
  cited itself.** Three consecutive entries called the single-cell `TypeError` "the highest-value
  known improvement to this artifact", each citing the previous entry rather than a measurement.
  It is worth **0 reward on both splits** (23/280 held-out rollouts hit it; 21 of the 23 pass).
  Meanwhile the actually-largest cluster — answer EXTENT, ≈5.7 held-out points across 20 tasks —
  was never named by anyone, because nobody had the held-out failure list. **Beliefs about leverage
  must be re-grounded in a measurement each iteration, or they calcify.** The same trap in its other
  form: `rejected.jsonl`'s rows were twice mis-read as "approach refuted" when the rejected
  candidate was an **empty diff** — always check the `diff.patch` (or its absence) before believing
  a rejection is about content.
- **What genuinely helped, mechanically.** (1) **Replaying the scorer's own code** instead of
  reading its feedback prose — that is what exposed the benchmark fault, and it also stopped me
  shipping a confidently-wrong int-vs-float "correction" that the feedback string was actively
  inviting. The two disagree, and only the code counts. (2) **Per-task diffing against the recorded
  seed baseline**, which revealed that the accepted prose *broke 9 held-out tasks* — a
  non-monotonicity that aggregate rewards (0.386 → 0.875) completely hide. (3) **Two read-only
  subagents in parallel**, with the explicit instruction to *verify or refute* rather than confirm:
