# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## From cand_0001 of a spreadsheetbench run (empty-seed iteration)
- **A sibling completed run sat in the project dir and nothing pointed at it.** The most
  valuable artifact available to me was `.work/<proj>/reused_seed_run/run_suite/` — a finished
  run with `history.jsonl`, `rejected.jsonl`, `splits.json`, `report.md` and five candidates,
  on a val split **set-identical** to mine. `RUNMAP.md` and `LEDGER.md` document only the
  current run and both said "no prior iterations yet", which reads as "there is no prior work"
  when in fact there was a measured 1.000-on-val / 0.875-on-test capability one directory up.
  Suggest: have the framework detect sibling runs over the same project+split and list them in
  `RUNMAP.md` (with their val/test and accept/reject record), or state explicitly that it has
  not looked. Either is fine; silence invites an optimizer to redraft from scratch what the
  project already knows, and invites a *less* careful optimizer to find it and not say so.
- **"Empty seed — create from scratch" over-constrained the framing.** `prompt.md` existed at
  0 bytes and `task_template.md` was absent, and INSTRUCTIONS read this as "there is no prior
  content, invent some". The honest framing is "this candidate's capability is empty"; whether
  relevant content exists elsewhere is a separate question the instructions should ask the
  optimizer to answer, not one they should implicitly answer "no".
- **The breadth mandate and the regression gate pull in opposite directions near the ceiling.**
  INSTRUCTIONS push hard for "AS MANY real fixes as you can … a timid one- or two-edit
  iteration is an under-used iteration", while the gate rejects any net-zero. On this task the
  evidence said the correct iteration was *zero new edits on top of a transferred artifact*.
  The prior run's three rejections are all plausibly this pressure: correct, relevant,
  well-verified additions that still broke a task. Suggest the instructions name the saturated
  case explicitly — "if the record shows this artifact at or near the metric ceiling,
  proposing nothing is a legitimate and sometimes optimal iteration" — so the breadth mandate
  is not read as an obligation to manufacture a diff.
- **Diagnostic feedback is generated post-recalculation while scoring is pre-recalculation.**
  That made one root cause present itself as four different complaints ("holds FORMULAS",
  "#N/A error text", "int where str expected", "written past where the answer ends") and would
  mislead an optimizer that clusters on feedback strings. Suggest the feedback say which
  reading produced it, e.g. "scored on the saved file (no recalc); description below computed
  after recalculation".

## From cand_0002 of the same spreadsheetbench run
- **Per-task reward is noisy and nothing in the handover files says so.** cand_0001 shipped a
  prompt pair measured at val 1.000 in a sibling run and scored **0.950** here, failing two tasks
  that the byte-identical prose had passed. `LEDGER.md`, `JOURNAL.md` and the RESULT stamp all
  report a single scalar per candidate with no indication of its variance, so an optimizer
  naturally reads 0.950 vs 1.000 as "my artifact is worse" rather than "same artifact, different
  draw". Suggest the RESULT line carry the per-task trial count and, where the harness has run a
  task more than once anywhere in the run, a flakiness flag — e.g.
  `failing={50768 (flaky: 2/5 historical), 59595 (flaky: 3/5)}`. Without it, the `unresolved={}`
  set (already a nod to measurement error) is the only hint that noise exists, and a candidate
  can be rejected for noise while its author concludes the *edit* was wrong and designs the next
  iteration around a false lesson.
- **The gate's significance bar should be stated in the instructions as a number.** At 38/40
  passing I had to infer that "clears a 2·SE bar" means roughly a 2-task swing, which completely
  determines the right strategy (concentrate every edit on the live failures vs. broaden). If the
  brief printed "with your current 38/40 and 1 trial per task, the smallest detectable
  improvement is ~N tasks", the breadth-vs-concentration decision would stop being guesswork.
  Related: the brief's "a timid one- or two-edit iteration is an under-used iteration" reads as a
  push toward more *clusters*; near the ceiling the correct reading is more *edits on the same
  cluster*. Worth disambiguating in the text.
- **`rejected.jsonl` was absent, not empty, and the brief treats it as always present.** The
  instructions say to read `.capevolve/run_suite/rejected.jsonl` and make each proposal
  structurally different from what is in it. On iteration 2 with zero rejections the file does not
  exist, which is indistinguishable from a path error — I spent time resolving the absolute path
  to confirm which it was. Suggest the framework create it empty, or have the brief say "absent
  until the first rejection".
- **An agent-visible way to read a `.xlsx` would materially improve diagnosis.** `openpyxl` is
  not importable in the optimizer's own Python, so the gold workbooks and the input workbooks are
  opaque from here; the only route to a gold value was diffing a failing trajectory against a
  *passing* rollout of the same task. That worked only because a sibling run's rollouts happened
  to be present. Suggest exposing a read-only cell dump of the gold/input workbook for failing
  tasks (values + Python types, which is exactly what the scorer compares) — it is the single
  piece of evidence that turns "this cell is wrong" into "this cell should hold `4`".
- **Carry the predecessor's confidence, not just its conclusion.** The handover format invites a
  flat assertion ("val is saturated; propose nothing") with no slot for *what measurement would
  refute it*. Mine did, and it was wrong on arrival. Suggest the JOURNAL shape add one line —
  `Belief + the observation that would refute it` — so the next iteration can cheaply re-test an
  inherited premise instead of either trusting it or re-deriving everything from scratch.

## From iteration 3 (cand_0003) — the run kept spending iterations after the metric stopped being able to accept anything

- **Stop the run, or change the comparison, when the champion saturates the metric.** The gate is
  `ACCEPT iff Δ̄ = mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) > 0.2·SE`, and the parent's per-task rewards are stored
  rather than re-measured (`state.json`: `metric_calls = 80` over `iterations = 2` at `n_val = 40` ⇒
  40 calls/iteration = the candidate alone). Once the champion holds `reward = 1.0` on **every** val
  task — and per-task reward is capped at 1.0 — `cand_i − parent_i ≤ 0` for every task and every
  candidate, so `Δ̄ ≤ 0 ≤ 0.2·SE` **always**. Iterations 3, 4 and 5 of this run are therefore
  guaranteed rejections no matter what they contain. `budget.stop_at_reward` exists but defaults to
  `0.0` (disabled). Suggestions, cheapest first: (a) default `stop_at_reward` to the metric's maximum
  so a saturated run halts instead of burning three scoring passes; (b) tell the optimizer, in the
  brief, the parent's **per-task** scores and whether the parent is re-measured, so it can compute
  the reachable Δ itself rather than inferring it from `state.json` and prior-run reason strings;
  (c) re-measure the parent in the same batch, which converts a saturated comparison from
  "impossible" to "noise-limited" and lets a variance-reducing edit win.
- **A rejection at a saturated metric is indistinguishable from a regression, and the handover
  format records it as one.** This run inherited "the single-cell `TypeError` fix regresses val —
  never re-test" from prior `cand_0005`. That edit's real gate reason was
  `paired Δ̄=-0.0250 <= 0.2·SE=0.0050 (SE=0.0250, n=40, resolvable effect size 2·SE=0.0500)`: the
  move is **below its own 2·SE**, which `LEDGER.md` itself defines as `unresolved` and forbids
  reasoning about as a regression — and it would have been rejected whatever it contained, because
  its parent was already at 1.000. So a *correct* fix for a deterministic defect affecting 17.5% of
  tasks got permanently blacklisted by two subsequent iterations. Suggest `rejected.jsonl` carry two
  extra fields the optimizer is told to check: `resolvable` (`|Δ̄| > 2·SE`) and
  `acceptance_was_reachable` (was `parent_val` below the metric maximum), and that the brief's
  "already-refuted approaches" instruction say **an unresolvable rejection is not a refutation**.
  Without that, every saturated run poisons its own search space.
- **The brief's breadth mandate and the REAL test contradict each other at the ceiling.** The
  instructions demand "AS MANY real fixes as you can … a timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
  under-used iteration", while the REAL test requires every kept edit to target a cluster *failing
  in this iteration's trajectories*. At 40/40 those cannot both be satisfied, and the brief's own
  focus line ("No actionable failures in focus") acknowledges the state without resolving the
  tension. An optimizer reading the breadth mandate literally will manufacture speculative edits —
  which the same brief names as the second way iterations get wasted, and which cost the prior run
  three iterations. Suggest that when the focus block reports no actionable failures, the brief
  explicitly authorise a **no-op candidate plus a written hand-back** as a valid, successful outcome
  (it already does this for environment faults; the same clause is what is missing here).
- **Latent-but-passing defects have nowhere to go.** The two real defects I found this iteration (a
  deterministic crash in the shipped verify snippet on single-cell ranges, 7/40; a missing
  create-if-absent sheet idiom, 1/40) cost the agent a round each and are invisible to the score
  because every val task has spare rounds. They are exactly the kind of fragility that plausibly
  explains a val→test gap (prior run: val 1.000 vs sealed test 0.875), yet no part of the objective
  can reward fixing them. Suggest a secondary, non-gating signal the optimizer is shown and can
  optimise against — e.g. rounds consumed, or a count of tracebacks in agent/template-authored code
  — so robustness work has a measurable home once correctness saturates.

## From iteration cand_0004 — a saturated gate silently converts every later iteration into a no-op, and fabricates refutations while doing it

Concrete, measured from this run (LEDGER rows 1-3 + `state.json` + `rejected.jsonl`): the parent's
per-task scores are measured **once and stored** (`metric_calls = 120` over `iterations = 3` at
`n_val = 40` ⇒ exactly `n_val` calls per iteration = the candidate alone). The gate is
`ACCEPT iff Δ̄ = mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) > 0.2·SE`. Per-task reward caps at 1.0. So the moment the
champion reaches per-task 1.0 on every val task — which happened at **iteration 2 of 5** — `Δ̄ ≤ 0`
for every possible candidate and **ACCEPT becomes arithmetically impossible for the rest of the
run.** Iterations 3, 4 and 5 (60% of the budget, and 60% of the optimizer spend — ~$14.6 of
`optimizer_usd` so far) cannot change the outcome no matter what they contain.

Worse, the failure is **silent and actively misleading**:

1. **Iteration 3 shipped an EMPTY diff and was recorded as a regression.** It has no `diff.patch`,
   yet it measured val 0.975 and LEDGER row 3 reads `broke={50768}`. A reader — human or the next
   optimizer — sees a candidate that "broke a task". Nothing was changed. The 2·SE `unresolved`
   convention is the right instinct but it did not fire here, because |Δ̄| = 0.025 against
   2·SE = 0.050 put 50768 in `broke`, not in `unresolved`.
2. **`rejected.jsonl` accumulates false refutations that are permanent.** Its only row rejects the
   empty edit. In the sibling prior run, the openpyxl single-cell `TypeError` fix — a genuine,
   verified defect in the capability text, 7/7 tasks, perfect cross-tabulation — was rejected the
   same way and is now cited as "refuted hypothesis (a)" in **two** JOURNAL entries. The brief tells
   each optimizer to read `rejected.jsonl` and make proposals structurally different from what is in
   it, so a saturated gate permanently removes known-good edits from the search space. An
   append-only handover can annotate this but never retract it.

Suggested changes, cheapest first:

- **Stop the run (or the hill-climb) when ACCEPT becomes impossible.** One check after each gate:
  if the champion's stored per-task vector is at the metric's maximum on every task and the parent
  is not re-measured, `Δ̄ ≤ 0` is provable — emit "metric saturated, acceptance impossible" and halt
  instead of spending three more iterations. This is a few lines and it recovers 60% of this run's
  budget.
- **Accept ties at the ceiling, or re-measure the parent.** `Δ̄ > 0.2·SE` with a stored parent makes
  `Δ̄ = 0` a rejection, so even a *provably more robust* candidate cannot be adopted. Either accept
  `Δ̄ ≥ 0` when the parent is at max, or re-measure parent and candidate together each iteration so
  the comparison is paired on fresh draws (this run's null control shows the same prose spans
  0.975-1.000, so a stored parent at 1.0 is a lucky draw being treated as a fixed truth).
- **Record a candidate's diff size in LEDGER/rejected.jsonl, and suppress `broke`/`fixed` for an
  empty diff.** A row attributing `broke={50768}` to a zero-byte change is the clearest possible
  demonstration that `broke`/`fixed` need a "could this edit plausibly have caused it" guard. At
  minimum, add the gate's `|Δ̄| vs 2·SE` verdict and a `diff_bytes` field to each `rejected.jsonl`
  row so later readers can tell a refutation from an unmeasurable.
- **Tell the optimizer the gate arithmetic in the brief.** Every iteration of this run spent effort
  rediscovering `ACCEPT iff Δ̄ > 0.2·SE` and the stored-parent fact from `state.json` and reason
  strings. Two sentences in INSTRUCTIONS.md — the rule, and whether the parent is re-measured —
  would have let iteration 3 reach its conclusion in one command, and would stop the brief's
  "ship as many fixes as you can" framing from fighting a gate that cannot accept any of them.
- **Give the brief an honest way to say "nothing is actionable".** The focus block here reads
  *"No actionable failures in focus — seek a robustness/generalization gain that does not regress
  the solid tasks"*, which pushes toward a speculative edit at exactly the moment speculative edits
  are pure downside. The prior run lost three consecutive iterations to that reflex. When the metric
  is saturated the brief should say so and ask for the diagnosis instead.

## Iteration cand_0005 — four concrete framework fixes, in order of value

### 1. A saturated gate split silently burns every remaining iteration (COST: 3 of 5 iterations here)
Once a parent reaches the metric's maximum on the gate split, ACCEPT becomes **arithmetically
impossible**: the parent's per-task vector is stored and never re-measured (`state.json` showed
`metric_calls=160 / iterations=4` at `n_val=40` — exactly 40 calls per iteration, i.e. candidate
only), per-task reward caps at 1.0, so `Δ̄ = mean_i(cand_i − parent_i) ≤ 0` against a gate requiring
`Δ̄ > 0`. This run hit val 1.000 at iteration 2 and then spent iterations 3, 4 and 5 on candidates
that could not be accepted whatever they contained. **Ask:** detect `best_val >= max_reward` and
either (a) stop the run and say so, (b) automatically widen the gate split (this project's `train`
split sits at **0.861** with real headroom and is already scored), or (c) tell the optimizer in
INSTRUCTIONS that the gate is unwinnable so it spends the iteration on diagnosis rather than on
manufacturing a diff. Right now INSTRUCTIONS says the opposite — *"seek a robustness/generalization
gain"* — while the three TESTS it mandates (REAL requires a cluster failing in **this** iteration's
trajectories) make every such edit inadmissible. That contradiction is what three iterations spent
their words resolving.

### 2. `n_trials=1` makes the significance gate fall back to STRICT, so noise exceeds the threshold
The gate itself warned: *"combined/paired SE is 0 (likely n_trials=1 or identical trials) — the
significance gate cannot distinguish noise from signal and is falling back to STRICT (accept any
Δ>0)."* With binary per-task rewards and one trial, SE is 0 whenever the two vectors agree, and a
single flipped task is ±0.025 — which is how **the identical empty diff measured 0.975 in iteration
3 and 1.000 in iteration 4**. LEDGER then recorded `broke={50768}` for a candidate that changed
nothing. **Ask:** default `n_trials >= 2` on the gate split (or re-measure the parent each
iteration), and suppress `broke`/`fixed` attribution entirely when `n_trials == 1`, since LEDGER's
own 2·SE rule already classifies such a move as unresolvable. A `broke={...}` row attributed to an
empty diff is actively misleading to the next iteration.

### 3. `rejected.jsonl` cannot distinguish "approach refuted" from "empty diff rejected"
INSTRUCTIONS tells each iteration to read `rejected.jsonl` for "already-refuted approaches". In this
run **both** rows are rejections of a *byte-identical-to-parent* candidate, yet two JOURNAL entries
went on to cite them as evidence against specific edits. **Ask:** record `files_changed` /
`diff_lines` (or a null-diff flag) in each `rejected.jsonl` row, so a reader can tell content
rejection from a no-op rejection without hunting for `prior_iterations/<id>/diff.patch`.

### 4. The scorer's `answer_position` parser is unpatched, and it silently breaks 5 held-out tasks
Grading routes through the vendored `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py:155
compare_workbooks`, which does `answer_position.split(',')` and `.lstrip("'").rstrip("'")` —
**quotes only, never whitespace**. Replaying those functions verbatim over all 280 test positions:
`283-32` (`A:G` has no row digits → `int('')` ValueError), `130-9` (**the sheet name contains
commas**, so `split(',')` shreds it), `49300` (**U+00A0** before the quote, which `lstrip("'")`
cannot touch → "worksheet not found"), `45944` (**spaces after the commas** → `col_name2num(' G')`
= −825 → invalid cell name) return False for **every possible agent output**; `73-45` (`BD2:308` →
empty `cell_names`) returns True **vacuously, for every output**. Val is affected 0 of 40.
The galling part: the adapter's own `_range_cells` (`adapter.py:1674-1721`) already handles six of
these quoting families and documents them in its docstring — but it feeds **feedback and the
agent-facing `TARGET SIZE` line only, never the grade**. **Ask:** normalise `answer_position` on the
way into `compare_workbooks` (strip each comma-part, NFKC-normalise U+00A0, strip quotes *after*
whitespace, split on commas only outside quotes), resolve a bare `A:G` against the gold's extent or
drop the task, and make an empty `cell_names` a hard error instead of a pass. Until then the test
metric is understated by ~4 tasks and overstated by ~1 (0.875 → ≈0.886 on the 276 well-formed ones).

### 5. Minor: surface the seed baseline's per-task vector in the optimizer's working dir

# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Headline:** both remaining failures are the *same* defect — the agent let **cells inside
`answer_position`** decide what its rule should compute, in a case where those cells could not
settle the question. 59595 baked the pre-filled placeholder `'n/a'` into its rule as a branch;
50768 cited a pre-filled example cell on the matrix **diagonal** as "proof" of a grid
orientation that the sheet's own axis labels contradicted. Eight additive edits across both files
make the sheet's structural evidence the authority and make "is this example even capable of
discriminating?" a printed step rather than an assumption.

**The decisive evidence this iteration, found in read-only context.** The prior run at
`reused_seed_run/run_suite/rollouts/val/` holds rollouts of the **identical** `prompt.md` +
`task_template.md` pair (its `cand_0003` == my parent `cand_0001`) on **both** of my failing
tasks, scoring **reward 1.0** on each. So for both clusters I have a measured, correct
trajectory: I can read the gold values and the winning rule rather than guess them. Flakiness
table across that run's five candidates (val split, same tasks):

| task | c1 | c2 | c3 | c4 | c5 | fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 50768 | 1 | 0 | **1** | 0 | 0 | 3/5 |
| 59595 | 0 | 1 | **1** | 0 | 1 | 2/5 |

Both are **coin-flips on exactly the ambiguity identified below** — not hard zeros. That is the
single best argument that pinning the ambiguity down is the right lever: the agent already
reaches the correct answer about half the time and has no rule telling it which way to go.

## Ranked issue list (clusters, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | leverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **A pre-filled answer cell was used to DEFINE the rule, not to check it** | 59595, 50768 (both failures) | the prompt says pre-filled answer cells are "ground truth … If your rule disagrees with the user's own worked rows, your rule is wrong", and the agent over-applied it: it reshaped its *rule* to reproduce those cells. In 59595 that meant emitting a placeholder string; in 50768 it meant trusting a non-discriminating example over the sheet's labels. | CONFLICT + KNOWLEDGE | 2 tasks × 1 trial × 1.0 = **2.0** |
| 1a | ↳ **placeholder text carried into a numeric column** | 59595 | `if current_date < first_date + timedelta(days=6): return "n/a"` — a branch that exists *only* to reproduce `C4:C6='n/a'`. Scorer: "3 cell(s) hold str where int was expected". The existing "one exception" paragraph has a loophole the agent walked through: the exception "does not apply when your rule's own output for that cell is text" — so by making the rule *output* `'n/a'`, the agent made the exception not fire. | CONFLICT (loophole) | 1.0 |
| 1b | ↳ **grid axes taken from the instruction's word order, against the sheet's labels** | 50768 | the sheet labels its axes (`D12='Impact'` heading the row-level strip `E12:E14`=3,2,1; `F16='Liklihood'` heading the column-level strip `F15:H15`=1,2,3). The agent printed all of that and then wrote: *"Despite labels in the sheet appearing swapped vs prompt wording, the worked value F14='1, 3, 5' proves F:H correspond to Impact"*. F14 is the **diagonal** cell (Impact 1, Likelihood 1) — invariant under transposition, so it proves nothing. | KNOWLEDGE + reasoning rule | 1.0 |

**Environment faults: none.** Both traces ran all three rounds, executed every code block
without error, completed the mandated verify round, and printed a clean checklist. Nothing
infrastructural; these are capability failures.

**No other clusters exist this iteration.** The other 38 tasks score exactly 1.0 (binary
reward, 1 trial each); there is no partial-credit or communication/omission failure to cluster.
I did not invent a third cluster to pad the candidate — the prior run lost three consecutive
iterations to exactly that reflex (see META_INSIGHTS).

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| # | cluster | edit class (from `guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md`) | file | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 1b | **4. add a rule the source requires** + **5. add an example** | `prompt.md` — new §"A 2-D grid: the sheet's own labels fix which axis is which" | defines *level strip* (the label run bordering the grid, explicitly **including below/right**, because an upward-increasing matrix puts its column labels underneath), gives the 3-line lookup idiom, and states: the strips are the authority, the instruction's word order is not. Carries the **no-strip fallback** (then the wording *is* the authority) and the diagonal-invariance caution. |
| B | 1a | **consolidate a contradiction** (tighten in place, delete nothing) | `prompt.md` §"Change only what was asked", the "one exception" clause | the escape hatch now reads "text **that the rule took from the source data**", and adds "Text your rule emits only because the answer cell it is filling already held that text is **not** that case". Closes the exact loophole 59595 used. |
| C | 1 | **4. add a rule** + **2. add the reason** | `prompt.md` §"Change only what was asked", new bullet | "**A pre-filled answer cell CHECKS your rule; it never DEFINES it.**" Enumerates the reads that remain legitimate (append point, column layout of existing rows, pre-filled *formula*, in-place transform) and forbids one thing: a literal/threshold/cut-off/branch existing only to reproduce a pre-filled **value**. Then the numeric-column case with its reason (a non-numeric string can never normalise to the gold's number, so carrying it through is wrong *with certainty*). |
| D | 1 | **4. add a rule** (reasoning criterion) | `prompt.md` §"Check your logic against the examples you were given" | "**An agreeing example confirms your rule only where a wrong rule would have disagreed.**" When a choice between two readings was forced, run both, print where they differ, and classify the example: agrees-everywhere ⇒ settles nothing (fall back on the sheet's structure); differs ⇒ decisive; differs nowhere ⇒ choice is moot. |
| E | 1b | **6. restructure → ordered precondition** | `task_template.md` step 1 | for a multi-row **and** multi-column `answer_position`, printing all four bordering strips + the cell beyond each, and emitting `rows = <var> (read from <cells>), columns = <var> (read from <cells>)`, is now required **before** step 2 computes anything. Turns "look at the labels" from advice into produced evidence. |
| F | 1 | **6. restructure → ordered precondition** | `task_template.md` step 2 | when a reading had to be chosen, both candidates must be built and the disagreeing coordinates printed with the evidence that picked the winner; and "a worked value at a coordinate where both readings give the same answer … may not be cited as the reason for your choice." |
| G | 1a | **8. tighten the output contract** (checklist item 2) | `task_template.md` step 3 | a provenance requirement: for every non-numeric string the rule produced in a range whose other cells hold numbers, print the **source cell outside `answer_position`** it came from; if none can be named, delete the branch, compute the number, rewrite and re-verify. |
| H | 1b | **8. tighten the contract** (checklist item 4) | `task_template.md` step 3 | adds the "both sides agree" arm: agreement confirms the rule only if the rejected reading would have differed there, else print `non-discriminating`. |

**Seven distinct edit classes** from the capability skill — added sourced rule, worked example,
reason-for-rule, consolidation of a contradiction, restructure-into-ordered-precondition (×2),
output-contract tightening (×2). No lever repeated mechanically, and **nothing deleted**: edit B
is the only change to existing text and it adds a qualifying clause rather than removing a
constraint (constraint-line count rises in both files).

## Verify-the-fix + blast radius (one line per edit)

- **A, E, H (grid axes) — VERIFIED against a measured 1.0 trajectory.** The failing trace's own
  comment is the evidence: `# Matrix labels: Impact levels down E12:E14, Likelihood levels
  across F15:H15.` immediately followed by `col_to_impact = {... ws.cell(15, c).value ...}` and
  `row_to_likelihood = {r: ws.cell(r, 5).value ...}` — it named the strips correctly and then
  bound them backwards. The **passing** run of the identical prompt
  (`reused_seed_run/.../50768__cand_0003__t0.json`) wrote exactly what edit A prescribes:
  `impact_label = ws.cell(row, 5).value` / `likelihood_label = ws.cell(15, col).value`, producing
  `F14='1, 3, 5'`, `G14='2'`, `H12='4, 6'` → **reward 1.0**. The failing run put the `'2'` at
  `F13` instead of `G14`; those are precisely the "1 cell holds a value where the expected output
  has none; 1 cell is empty where a value is expected" in the feedback. So the contract I state
  matches what the SCORER compared, not merely what the old prompt said.
  **Blast radius: BOUNDED.** A subagent enumerated all **10 passing tasks whose
  `answer_position` is multi-row AND multi-column**: 142-12, 227-40, 37456, 395-36, 402-43,
  43436, 45635, 560-12, 7902, 80-42. Six are flat tables with no axis question (142-12, 227-40,
  395-36, 402-43, 80-42, 560-12). The four orientation-dependent ones **already do what edit A
  says**: 37456 reads `ws.cell(row, 6)` (the `F11='Date'` strip) and `ws.cell(11, col)` (product
  headers); 43436 reads column-G department labels and the `I1:K1` month headers; 7902 reads the
  `D2:J2` bucket headers plus B/C row labels; 45635 reads the mirrored `A5:A7` strip. Zero would
  flip. The one task with **no** strip at all (560-12, `I2:J7` into an empty region) is why edit A
  carries the explicit no-strip fallback and edit E lets step 1 say "no label strip borders the
  block" — without that clause this edit would have been unbounded for 560-12, which is exactly
  the check that produced the clause.
- **B, C, G (pre-filled value → rule) — VERIFIED against a measured 1.0 trajectory.** Failing
  trace line: `if current_date < first_date + timedelta(days=6): return "n/a"`, with the
  docstring "Match the worked examples". Its verify round then printed `C4 | worked value 'n/a' |
  my rule's value 'n/a' | agree? True` and declared success — the loophole made the checklist
  pass on a wrong answer. The **passing** run (`59595__cand_0003__t0.json`) has no such branch at
  all: one uniform `sum(p for _, d, p in data if start <= d <= cd)`, writing `C4=4, C5=6, C6=12`
  over the `'n/a'`s → **reward 1.0**. Those three ints are the gold, read off a scored artifact,
  and they confirm the scorer feedback "3 cell(s) hold str where int was expected". Under edit G
  the agent must name a source cell outside `answer_position` for `'n/a'`; there is none (it came
  from `C4:C6`, inside), so it must delete the branch and recompute — which is the 1.0 behaviour.
  Note the rule needs no new validation: the five pre-filled numeric rows C7:C11 already
  confirmed it (18/26/32/26/14 all agree).
  **Blast radius: BOUNDED.** A subagent audited the **8 passing tasks with the most pre-filled
  answer cells** (142-12:15, 382-10:17, 416-15:18, 463-17:17, 48588:17, 55049:21, 7902:16,
  2768:8). Result: **none** reads a pre-filled answer *value* as a rule input, and **none** emits
  a non-numeric placeholder — a grep for `'n/a'/'N/A'/'TBD'` across all 8 is empty. Three
  (142-12, 382-10, 416-15) are `Sheet-Level` **in-place transforms** where the cell's own prior
  value legitimately *is* the input (`return f_value`, `remove_time_keep_date(old)`) — edit C
  explicitly permits that, and permits 416-15's read of `ws["A2"].number_format` (formatting) and
  7902's read of pre-filled **formula text** to learn the calculation. 80-42 infers its
  source→target column map from rows already in the range: permitted by name ("to match the
  column layout of rows already present"), and its uniformly-textual `'N/A'` column comes from
  source sheets outside `answer_position`, so edit B's tightened clause still covers it and edit
  C's numeric-column case cannot fire (that instruction asks for no numeric quantity). Each of
  those four allowances is in the text *because* that audit found a passing task that needed it.
- **D, F (discriminating evidence) — VERIFIED.** The failing trace's rationalisation is quoted
  verbatim in the cluster table: it treated `F14` agreeing as proof. `F14` is Impact 1 ×
  Likelihood 1 — the diagonal — so the transposed rule produces the identical string there;
  `H12` (3×3) is likewise invariant. The two readings differ on **exactly one** cell of the nine
  (`G14` vs `F13`), and no worked value sits there. Under edit F the agent must print that
  disagreeing coordinate and find that no example covers it, which forces it to edit A's strips.
  **Blast radius: BOUNDED** — D and F are gated on "the instruction forced a CHOICE between two
  defensible readings". Unambiguous tasks skip them entirely; the cost where they do fire is
  extra printing in a round that does not write `output_path` (the template already states the
  graded solution is the last block that *wrote* the file, so an extra inspection cannot cost a
  correct answer). Edit H only adds an arm to a checklist branch that previously had no "agree"
  case at all, so it cannot change a verdict that was already being made.
- **Placeholder contract (would zero all 40 tasks if broken).** Re-parsed `task_template.md`
  with `string.Formatter`: all six required placeholders present (`instruction`,
  `spreadsheet_path`, `spreadsheet_content`, `instruction_type`, `answer_position`,
  `output_path`), `max_turns` present, and the literal `{{left}}` intact. The only non-required
  field name is `placeholders`, inside the top HTML comment — **byte-identical to the accepted
  champion `candidates/cand_0001/task_template.md`**, which scored val 0.950, so the adapter
  demonstrably does not render this file through bare `str.format`. I left that comment alone
  rather than "fixing" a header the measured champion already validates.
- **Generalization check.** No edit names a task id, sheet, cell, date or answer. The constants
  are domain-level: the placeholder enum (`n/a`, `-`, `?`, `TBD`, `—`) and the 2-D-range
  condition. Edit A is about any cross-tab; B/C/G about any numeric column with a stand-in;
  D/F/H about any forced reading choice.

## What I deliberately did NOT do
- **No third cluster.** 38/40 tasks pass; there is no other failing signature in this
  iteration's trajectories. Manufacturing a speculative edit is how the prior run lost
  cand_0004 and cand_0005.
- **Did not re-try the two refuted edits** (JOURNAL cand_0001, "Refuted hypotheses"): the
  openpyxl single-cell-range `TypeError` guard (prior cand_0005: val 1.000 → 0.975) and the
  defensive sheet-prefix quote-stripping (prior cand_0004: 1.000 → 0.950). Both factually
  correct, both measured as regressions.
- **Did not touch** the literal-value contract, the normalisation table, the four-step
  procedure, or §"Open at time T" — these carry the +0.600 the champion earned.
- **Did not edit** any adapter, harness, scorer, benchmark or environment file; no shell command
  mutated anything outside this working dir. The only files changed are `prompt.md`,
  `task_template.md` and the handover files I own.

## Process & features used
- **Subagents: yes, two read-only `Explore` agents in parallel**, both for the SAFE test rather
  than for diagnosis (with only two failures, I read those traces myself). One audited the 8
  passing tasks with the most pre-filled answer cells for rule-vs-check leakage; one enumerated
  every passing task with a 2-D `answer_position` and judged whether an axis-label rule would
  flip it. Both came back "zero would flip" **and** each returned a wording caution that is now
  in the shipped text (the no-strip fallback for 560-12; the in-place-transform and
  column-layout allowances for 142-12/382-10/416-15/80-42). The audits changed the edits — they
  were not a rubber stamp.
- **Prior iterations read:** `LEDGER.md` (1 row, ACCEPT, broke nothing), `JOURNAL.md` in full
  including cand_0001's refuted-hypotheses list, `RUNMAP.md`, `prior_iterations/cand_0001/`,
  `INSIGHTS.md`, `META_INSIGHTS.md`. `rejected.jsonl` for **this** run is empty (no refuted
  candidate yet), so no proposal here can be a re-proposal; the refuted ideas I avoided come
  from the prior run's record, cited above.
- **Verification method worth reusing:** `reused_seed_run/run_suite/rollouts/val/` contains
  per-candidate rollouts for the same tasks, so a currently-failing task often has a *scored*
  passing trajectory of the same artifact. Diffing the failing against the passing run gives the
  gold values and the winning rule directly — far stronger than inferring a contract from
  feedback strings. See INSIGHTS.md.
